description:
## Why
Elixir has none of these, so the five fixtures that call them keep twins: 01582 (Kernel.range/3), 01629 (Kernel.compare/2), 01623 (String.index_of/2), 01625 (String.to_byte_list/1), 01619 (List.reverse/2). Callers outside those fixtures, measured on origin/develop 9754e64d9 (doc examples excluded):
- Kernel.compare/2: lib/kernel.fz's <, <=, >, >= (1226, 1259, 1295, 1328) and lib/enum.fz 746, 1100, 1160, 1179. Docs that name it: .agent/docs/externs.md:130, .agent/docs/semantic-authorities.md:119.
- String.index_of/2: lib/option_parser.fz:284; inside lib/string.fz, contains?/2 (680) and lines 742 and 775.
- String.to_byte_list/1: only its own recursion.
- List.reverse/2: no lib caller; a comment at src/compiler2/types/arrow_match_test.rs:146 names its spec.
- Kernel.range/3: no caller.

## Files
lib/kernel.fz, lib/enum.fz, lib/string.fz, lib/list.fz, lib/option_parser.fz, the two .agent docs above, src/compiler2/types/arrow_match_test.rs (comment), and fixtures 01582, 01619, 01623, 01625, 01629. lib/enum.fz is also being edited by fz-sc8.245 (to_list, ~156): different lines, and whichever lands second rebases.

## Decide with the owner
- Retire (Elixir): each becomes a private lib helper (or goes away where lib does not need it), and fixtures spell the Elixir equivalent: `a..b//s` or Range.new/3; `<`/`==` term ordering; :binary.match/2; :binary.bin_to_list/1; Enum.reverse/2. Then each fixture is wrapped in defmodule Main with `# oracle: self` and its twin deleted.
- Keep them as fz extensions: the five keep twins and are listed by the fixtures.md ticket.

## Known per-fixture facts
- 01623 also calls Kernel.assert/2, which is fz-only too (39 fixtures use assert). The conversion prints its checked values instead. Retiring assert is a separate decision.
- 01623's subject is the zero-width match; Erlang's :binary.match raises badarg on an empty pattern, so the converted fixture states whatever Elixir does there.
- 01619 also needs `when a: var` on `@spec rev([a], [a]) :: [a]` (Elixir: type a/0 undefined), which fz-nhb.11 makes readable.

## Signal
Retire: none of the five names is public in lib/; five fewer twins; full gate green.
title: fz's stdlib exposes Elixir's names only: Kernel.range/3, Kernel.compare/2, String.index_of/2, String.to_byte_list/1 and List.reverse/2 leave the public surface
